aggregatedMarking.description: The effective markings rolled up into one marking by the target scheme. Empty when no rule contributed, or when the result spans more than one target scheme, in which case `aggregatedMarkings` holds one per scheme.

aggregatedMarkings.description: Aggregated output keyed by target scheme id. Present when guide evaluation routed through more than one target scheme.

breakdown.description: One entry per evaluated rule: for each guide, its selected rules, then its computed rules.

contributingBreakdown.description: Subset of `breakdown` that actually contributed to `aggregatedMarking` (i.e. `breakdown.filter(b => !b.wasOverridden)`). Precomputed so UI layers stop re-filtering the full breakdown.

effectiveMarkings.description: The marking each contributing rule's outcome resolves to. Overridden rules contribute none.

guideId.description: The id of the guide evaluated. Absent when the result combines several guides.

provenance.description: External guide-rule source observation used by this evaluation.

selectedRules.description: The selected rules that were evaluated. Rules with a `when` condition are computed, not selected, and are not listed here.

ExplanationTrace.description:
Full pipeline trace for one marking: parse input, repairs applied, inferences drawn, validation errors, and the final output.

What `explain` returns, and nothing else. It takes what `process` takes and answers why the engine settled the marking the way it did, step by step. No other result carries it, because their callers want the answer rather than the working. Debug tools use this to explain why a marking was accepted or rejected. `repairs` lists each repair rule that fired and the before/after strings. `inferences` lists each inference rule that added a concept and the reason text.

entries.description: Every step the pipeline took, in the order it took them.

finalAssertions.description: The assertions the pipeline settled on, listed in print order as a validate result's `assertions` are.

inferences.description: Each concept an inference rule added, in the order added.

input.description: The marking text the explanation was asked for, as given.

rendered.description: The settled marking, written in the output format.

repairs.description: Each repair rule that rewrote the input, in the order applied.

schemeId.description: The id of the scheme the marking was read against.

validationErrors.description: The constraints the settled marking violates.

Fix.description:
One way to make the marking valid. Every change in it answers an error.

A fix is a whole marking, not a patch: `rendered` is the complete marking the author would end up with. The engine proves each one before offering it: it reads the marking back, judges it the way it judges any input, and offers only those that read back valid.

adds.description: Concepts this fix adds because an error requires them.

keeps.description: Concepts of the author's marking this fix keeps.

message.description: What this fix does, in words.

removes.description: Concepts of the author's marking this fix removes because an error names them.

rendered.description:
The valid marking this fix produces, in the result's output format.

It is written exactly as the result's own `rendered` is, so the two can be shown side by side. On an in-process engine with an `afterRender` plugin, that includes the plugin; the proof reads back the engine's own writing from before the plugin ran, so the plugin never decides which fixes are offered.

FixAction.description: Discrete mutation represented by an engine `Change`.

FixConceptReference.description: Stable reference to a concept a fix or change touches.

GuideBreakdownEntry.description: Per-rule breakdown in a guide evaluation result.

isComputed.description: Whether the rule was activated from other guide facts.

outcome.description: Rule outcome evaluated by the guide engine.

overriddenBy.description: Qualified overriding rule when this outcome was replaced.

rule.description: Qualified rule whose outcome was evaluated.

wasOverridden.description: Whether an active rule replaced this rule's outcome.

GuideCompilationStatus.description: Closed status of the analyst-determined guide compilation dimension.

GuideCompiledDetail.description: Full guide and scheme breakdown retained by the full response profile.

process.description: What validate answers for the compiled assertions: the facts settled, whether they stand, and why not. A compiled marking is checked, not corrected, so it carries no fix paths.

GuideCompiledResult.description: Deterministic guide compilation for one authority basis and unit.

assertions.description: Effective compiled assertions, listed in print order as a validate result's are.

computedRules.description: Computed rules contributing to the result.

detail.description: Complete evaluation and process breakdown for the full profile.

directRules.description: Direct rules contributing to the result.

rendered.description: Scheme-rendered marking for the compiled assertions.

supportIds.description: References into the evaluation support catalog.

valid.description: Whether the compiled marking stands once settled, as `ValidateResult.valid` defines it.

GuideContentEvaluation.description: Complete evidence and compilation result for document guide evaluation.

documentDigest.description: Digest of the exact evaluated document bytes.

units.description: Compilation results for the document and authored parts.

GuideFactKind.description: Authority state of a fact used by guide compilation.

GuideFactReference.description: Joins assertion support to the guide fact that supplied its authority.

kind.description: Authority state of the referenced guide fact.

GuideFindingDecision.description: Analyst determination for a nominated guide finding.

GuideFindingDetermination.description: Records an explicit analyst decision about one lexical nomination.

decision.description: Analyst decision for the nominated occurrence.

documentDigest.description: Digest of the exact document revision reviewed.

findingId.description: Stable identifier of the exact nominated occurrence.

proposalOrigin.description: Optional provenance for how the decision proposal was drafted.

GuideMatchSpec.description: A named pattern matcher specification. Use built-in types like 'ipv4', 'email', 'coordinates', or 'regex' with a custom pattern.

caseSensitive.description: Case-sensitivity for a `type: 'regex'` leaf. When true the pattern compiles without the `i` flag, so an `[A-Z]` class means uppercase only. Absent or false, the pattern matches case-insensitively. Ignored on non-`regex` leaves.

label.description: Display label: overrides the matcher's built-in label.

pattern.description: Custom regex pattern: only used when type is 'regex'.

runtime.description: `runtime: true` marks a matcher provided by the host at runtime. Such a leaf is always valid at load; if the named matcher is not registered it matches nothing here, and resolves normally where it is registered.

type.description: Matcher type: a built-in name (ipv4, cidr, ipv6, mac_address, email, hostname, url, coordinates, mgrs, phone, ssn, credit_card, date, uuid) or 'regex' for custom. Domain-specific packs (usgov, healthcare, financial, ...) add further names when registered.

GuideNomination.description: Evidence-preserving lexical nomination requiring analyst review.

documentDigest.description: Digest of the exact scanned document bytes.

findingId.description: Deterministic identity of this evidence occurrence.

origin.description:
Nomination source; lexical evidence is never authoritative itself.

Always `lexical`, and fixed for this major version. A nomination is by definition a rule's evidence matched in the document text, and the counts, determinations and advisory results that refer to nominations all mean lexical ones. A proposal from any other source (an analyst, an agent, a host) reaches the analyst as a manual selection with its own `proposalOrigin`. A new nomination source would change what this list means, so it would arrive as a new field, not as a new value here.

proposedAssertions.description: Assertions the rule would propose if accepted.

rule.description: Qualified rule nominated by the evidence.

GuideRule.description:
A rule in a marking guide: a data-element description with an outcome that contributes to the aggregate marking when activated.

Rules are presented as checkboxes in the UI. `keywords` enables keyword-search filtering; `match` enables text-scan detection (e.g., finding IPv4 addresses in a document body). `outcome.rendered` or `outcome.concepts` provides the marking contribution. Rules with `when` are computed; they auto-activate based on sibling rule selection state and do not appear as user-visible checkboxes.

This is the named runtime/read-result shape. Authoring input is carried by the guide definition's `rules.inline` entries.

category.description: Guide category ID for grouping in the UI.

description.description: Description of the data element this rule covers.

keywords.description: Searchable terms for literal keyword filtering (absent on computed rules).

match.description: Named pattern matchers for content evaluation. Each entry is a `MatchNode`: a leaf spec referencing a built-in matcher (e.g. `{ type: 'ipv4' }`) or a custom regex (`{ type: 'regex', pattern: '...' }`), or a combinator node (`any` / `all` / `not` / `near` / `context` / `validate`) composed over child nodes. When content is evaluated, both `keywords` and `match` are checked.

outcome.description: What this rule contributes when active. At least one of rendered or concepts must be set.

overrides.description: Rule IDs whose outcomes this rule replaces when active. When omitted (default), this rule's outcome is additive: it contributes alongside the rules it depends on.

rationale.description: Explanation of why this outcome applies.

when.description: When present, this rule auto-activates based on other rules' selection state. Uses the same when framework as scheme rules. `has` references guide rule IDs. Rules with `when` are "computed"; they don't appear as checkboxes.

GuideRuleOutcome.description: The effect of a guide rule: what it contributes to the marking.

concepts.description: Direct concept references: converted to assertions, then engine.process()'d.

rendered.description: Pre-rendered marking string: parsed by engine.process() during evaluation.

GuideScanResult.description:
A guide rule matched by text scanning, with every span where the rule's keywords or matchers fired. Returned by the engine's `scanGuides` and the standalone `scanTextForRules` / `scanMultipleGuides` helpers.

Parallels the scheme-side scan result: one entry per rule hit, with offsets into the scanned text.

guideId.description: The id of the guide the rule belongs to, when the scan covered more than one.

matchedKeywords.description: Each keyword or matcher label that fired, once each.

provenance.description:
Source provenance for the guide-rule source that supplied the matched rule.

Populated only when the rule came from an external `GuideRuleSource` override wired into the `GuideEngine` at load time (typically a `MappedGuideRuleSource` the server's Context loader built from a guide YAML's `rules.external` block). Inline-backed results leave this field undefined to keep payloads compact for the common single-source case.

Identity fields mirror the source's `sourceIdentity()` observation at engine-construction time.

spans.description: Every place in the text where the rule fired, in the order found.

GuideScanSpan.description: A span, by offsets into the scanned text, where a guide rule keyword or pattern matched.

confidence.description: Advisory confidence in [0, 1], present only when the scan asked for it with the `confidence` scan option. An ordinal hint derived from the match's shape, not a calibrated probability.

end.description: Offset in the scanned text just past the end of the match, in UTF-16 code units.

keyword.description: The keyword that matched, or the label of the matcher that did.

start.description: Offset in the scanned text where the match starts, in UTF-16 code units.

GuideScopeCoverage.description: Coverage of one unit against determined and projected requirements.

projectedCoverage.description: Advisory coverage assuming unresolved nominations are accepted.

GuideUnitEvaluation.description: Determined and projected compilation for one document unit.

determined.description: Compilation over accepted findings and manual selections.

findingIds.description: Nomination IDs whose evidence belongs to this unit.

projected.description: Advisory compilation additionally assuming unresolved nominations.

InputSpan.description: One span of the input, by offset and text.

end.description: End offset in the input string.

start.description: Start offset in the input string.

ManualGuideSelection.description: Validated manual guide fact bound to a document revision.

documentDigest.description: Digest of the exact document revision reviewed.

evidence.description: Evidence in the submitted document supporting the selection.

proposalOrigin.description: Optional provenance for how the selection proposal was drafted.

rule.description: Qualified loaded rule selected by the analyst.

MarkingValidation.description:
How an audit judged one authored marking, whole or part.

`valid` and `inputWasValid` mean exactly what `ValidateResult` defines them to mean. An audit asks whether the marking was right as the author wrote it, and that is `inputWasValid`; `valid` says whether it stands once the engine has settled it, as it does everywhere else.

It carries the marking's facts and how far recognition got with it, so a caller that rolls markings up, checks access or offers a correction works from the audit instead of reading each marking a second time.

appliedFixes.description: Every change the engine made while settling the marking, as `ValidateResult.appliedFixes`. Empty when it made none, so a false `inputWasValid` is always explained here or in `errors`.

assertions.description: The facts the marking states, settled and listed in print order as a validate result's `assertions` are, in the role the marking has in this document.

errors.description: What the scheme's rules find wrong with the settled marking.

inputWasValid.description: Whether the marking needed no change as written, as `ValidateResult.inputWasValid`.

proposedFixes.description: The ways to make the marking valid, each a whole marking the engine has read back and found valid, as `ProcessResult.proposedFixes`. An audit offers them because its caller is usually the author about to fix the document.

recognition.description: What recognition made of the marking, as `ValidateResult.recognition`.

rendered.description: The settled marking, written as validate writes it when the request names no output: in the scheme's default format, or for a scheme that declares `render.surfaces`, each written surface in its default for the role the marking has in this document, by the rule `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states.

valid.description: Whether the marking stands once settled, as `ValidateResult.valid`.

MatchAllNode.description: The `all` combinator: every child must match, and all children must overlap within `within` of the first child's span. The emitted span is the first child's (the anchor). Used to require several signals co-occur.

all.description: The signals that must all match. The first is the anchor whose span is kept.

label.description: Display label for this node's matches. Defaults to `all`.

within.description: How close every other child's match must lie to the anchor's.

MatchAnyNode.description: The `any` combinator: a union of child spans under one label. Used to express a multi-format value as several small, individually screened leaves instead of one giant alternation.

any.description: The alternatives. A span any of them matches is a match.

label.description: Display label for this node's matches. Defaults to `any`.

MatchContextExpression.description: Cue relationship used by the context combinator.

candidate.description: The spans to keep when the cue is present.

cue.description: The span that must lie near a candidate for it to count.

side.description: Where the cue may lie relative to the candidate: `before`, `after`, or `both` (the default).

within.description: How close the cue must lie to the candidate.

MatchContextNode.description: The `context` combinator: keep each `candidate` span only when a `cue` span lies within `within` on the given `side` (default `both`). Used to require a positive cue (e.g. a ZIP only counts with a postal/state cue nearby).

context.description: The candidate and the cue it needs.

label.description: Display label for this node's matches. Defaults to `context`.

MatchContextSide.description: Relative position accepted by a context-expression cue.

MatchNearEmit.description: Span emitted by a near-expression match.

MatchNearExpression.description: Pairing expression used by the near combinator.

a.description: The first span of the pair. Kept by default.

b.description: The second span of the pair.

emit.description: Which span survives a match: `a` (the default), `b`, or `envelope`, the span covering both.

within.description: How close the `b` span must lie to the `a` span.

MatchNearNode.description: The `near` combinator: pair an `a` span with a `b` span that lies within `within`. `emit` selects which span survives: the `a` span (default), the `b` span, or the envelope spanning both.

label.description: Display label for this node's matches. Defaults to `near`.

MatchNode.description: A declarative match expression: a `GuideMatchSpec` leaf, or one of the combinator nodes composed over child nodes. A guide rule's `match` array is a list of these.

MatchNotNode.description: The `not` combinator: keep each `of` candidate span only when NO `not` span lies within `within` of it. Drops a candidate that has a competing cue nearby.

label.description: Display label for this node's matches. Defaults to `not`.

not.description: The competing cue. A candidate with one of its spans nearby is dropped.

of.description: The candidate spans to keep or drop.

within.description: How close a `not` span must lie to a candidate to drop it.

MatchValidateNode.description: The `validate` combinator: run the named validator over each `candidate` span's matched text and keep the candidate when the validator passes (`keep: 'pass'`, the default) or when it fails (`keep: 'fail'`). The validator is content-free arithmetic or structure registered in the validator registry; an unknown name is a load-time error.

label.description: Display label for this node's matches. Defaults to `validate`.

validate.description: The validator to run and which outcome to keep.

MatchValidationExpression.description: Validator invocation used by the validate combinator.

args.description: Optional opaque arguments passed through to the validator.

candidate.description: The spans whose matched text the validator checks.

keep.description: Which outcome keeps a candidate: `pass` (the default) or `fail`.

MatchValidationKeep.description: Validator outcome retained by a validation expression.

NoticeViewValues.description:
The value a notice is registered under, keyed by view name, e.g. `{ ism: 'RD' }`.

Structurally the same map as `ViewLabels` and deliberately not the same type. A view label is how a view spells something for a reader; this is the token a view's own vocabulary files the notice under, and one is never substitutable for the other.

appliedFixes.description:
Every change the engine actually made while settling the marking: a departure from canonical spelling or order that recognition read through, a repair, a fact a rule required, a handed-in fact settling removed, or text read in the other role from the one the request names. A removed fact is named with the reason it was removed, including a fact handed in with a derived source label that the run does not derive again. A requirement that conflicts with an existing concept is not added and appears in errors and proposed fixes, with no applied change. Repair never removes an author-stated concept. These are the reasons a marking can be `valid` while `inputWasValid` is false.

A departure from spelling or order is reported here without a position. On a process result, `recognition.corrections` reports the same departure with the span of the text it covers. They are one change seen two ways, so a display shows one of them, not both. The role departure, `_recognition_role`, is about the whole text: it has no span and no entry in `recognition.corrections`, so it is reported only here, and a display that shows corrections in place of this list still shows it.

assertions.description:
The facts the marking states, as the engine settled them.

Listed in print order: the order the rendered marking places each concept; a concept the rendering leaves out appears where it would print. A concept the rendering has no place for at all follows the others of its category, or comes last when its category has none, in the order the scheme declares.

assertionsBeforeRepair.description:
What was read before repair: the assertions the input stated, before the repair pass took anything away or rewrote it. A retired concept appears under its replacement's name, as it does in `assertions` and in the fixes.

Present only when repair rewrote something that was read. Absent, everything read came through repair. This is a record of the reading; proposed fixes are computed against the resulting `assertions`, never against this earlier set. Repair leaves author-stated rule conflicts in the resulting value for the author to resolve.

Listed in print order, placed by the same rendering as `assertions`. A concept repair took away has no place in it, so it follows the others of its category.

assessment.description: The assessment of `rendered`: what it wrote of these facts, what it left out, what collapsed into an equivalent, and what it could not write at all. When `rendered` carries more than one surface, this is the combined assessment `RenderResult` describes. Read it before treating `rendered` as a transport.

displayColor.description: Portable scheme-derived display color for the settled marking. Embedding hosts may override this presentation default.

errors.description:
What the scheme's rules find wrong with the settled marking. An entry whose severity is `error` makes `valid` false.

No entry here points at a fix path: `suggestedFix` is set only on a result that carries the fix it names, and this result carries none.

inputWasValid.description:
True when the text or facts as given needed no change to stand.

Defined here once, and judged after the same settling as `valid`. A marking can be `valid` without having been valid as given: the engine settled it into one that stands. A result whose `inputWasValid` is false always says why: each change the engine made is in `appliedFixes`, and whatever it could not settle is in `errors`.

Right as written is judged against the view the text was read as, the one `recognition.inputFormat` reports, or for text read on more than one surface, the view each surface's part was read as. A fact settling adds, including a restored tier parent, counts against it only when that view writes the fact. A view that leaves the fact out writes the same text with the fact as without it, so the text was right already. Text read as no single view counts the fact when any view that read it writes it. Facts handed in with no text are judged against what a request that names no output writes them in, by the rule `rendered` follows.

Text is also not right as written when the request's context names a role and recognition decided the text is a view of the other role, as `recognition.role` reports. The result carries that departure in `appliedFixes` under `_recognition_role`, and `valid` is judged as it would be without it. A request that names its input format has said which view the text is: the text is judged as that view, and no role departure is raised. On a scan region and on a marking a document audit judges, the role the marking's place gives it stands for the context's role: a region found inside a wrapper is a part, and an audit judges each marking in the role it has in the document.

notices.description: The notices the scheme attaches to the concepts in `assertions`, collected the same way `SchemeEngine.collectNotices()` collects them. Always present, empty when the marking carries none, so a consumer can read the field without checking that it exists.

proposedFixes.description:
The ways to make the resulting value valid, computed from that value after applied changes, each a whole marking the engine has read back and found valid before offering it. Empty when the marking is valid, or when no change the engine could prove would make it so. An error's `suggestedFix` names one of these by its `message`.

A request's `parts` go back in with each fix, as the caller will send them, so they are read again in the fix's whole and the fix is judged with them: every part that read as a valid part marking in the call still does, and the fix covers every part that does. A part that did not read as a valid part marking in the call is one no fix to the whole can mend, so it does not keep a fix from being offered, and it may still fail beside the fix.

Proofs spend what is left of the call's work budget. When a proof runs out of it, or the caller cancels the call, the paths not yet proven are not offered, and `warnings` carries a notice whose `ruleId` is `_fixes_unproven`, so a short list or an empty one is not taken for every fix there is.

recognition.description: What recognition made of the text, with the corrections that turn it into canonical text. Present exactly when there was text to recognize.

rendered.description:
The settled marking, in one string.

It is written in the output the request names. With none named, a scheme without `render.surfaces` writes its default format, and a scheme with them writes each surface in its default for the marking's role, by the rule `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states. Every operation that returns this shape follows that one rule.

For a scheme that declares `render.surfaces`, the string is the output resolved on each surface the result writes, as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` describes, in declared surface order and joined by `render.surface_separator`. An output that writes nothing adds nothing, and outputs written as XML attributes in one namespace merge into one attribute list. One refused output refuses the whole string, and `assessment` says which one and why.

renders.description:
The outputs the request named in `outputs`, one entry each, keyed by output address. Empty when the request named none.

A host that binds one marking to fields written in different outputs names those outputs and gets every one from a single call. An output that could not write the state is present and says so in its assessment, because an output that refused to write a state is a different fact from one nobody asked for.

suggestionsFor.description:
The options for each category the request named in `suggestFor`, answered against these settled facts exactly as `suggestForCategories` answers them, in the request's output format and surface.

Computed only when asked. Present when the request named `suggestFor`, with one entry per category named; absent otherwise. It is how a composer keystroke gets the reading and the next picker's options in one round trip instead of two.

valid.description:
True when the marking stands once the engine has settled it: read, repaired, completed by what the scheme's rules imply, and judged with no error left.

Defined here once, and every result that reports `valid` means this, whichever operation produced it and whichever door it came through. Reading is tolerant on purpose, so the engine settles what it can. Whether the text was right as written is what `inputWasValid` and `appliedFixes` answer; no request asks the engine to settle less, so validate and process give the same `valid` for the same input, context, surface and parts.

warnings.description: Advisories that do not affect `valid`, such as a deprecated concept. On a process result whose fix paths were not all proven, this carries a notice whose `ruleId` is `_fixes_unproven`, as `ProcessResult.proposedFixes` describes.

ProcessingRole.description: Structural role of a marking within a processing operation.

RecognitionCorrection.description: One span recognition rewrote, with what it was and what it became.

end.description: End offset in the input string.

reason.description: What kind of departure from canonical this was.

replacement.description: The canonical text it was read as.

start.description: Start offset in the input string.

RecognitionCorrectionReason.description:
Why recognition rewrote one span of the input on the way to a reading.

`alias` covers a concept read in a spelling the reading form does not write, the spelling another of the concept's views gives among them, and a prefix read in one of its `prefix_aliases`. The replacement is the spelling the form writes.

RecognitionLimit.description:
The ceilings recognition can reach.

Closed, because a caller distinguishing a cancelled run from an exhausted one is writing a branch, not a message. `aborted` is the caller's own `AbortSignal` firing, which is a ceiling in the sense that matters here: the answer is not a confident one. `wall-clock` is the operator's time limit, and it is a separate word from `transitions` because the two say different things to whoever set them: one means the input was harder than the work ceiling allows, the other that the host was slower than the time allowed or the input harder than both.

RecognitionResult.description:
What recognition made of an input string: how far it got, what it read, and what it could not account for.

Every character of the marking region is accounted for: `complete` means recognized content, declared syntax, or permitted whitespace, with nothing left over. Finding one field is never enough to stop reading. An input that supports two distinct readings is `ambiguous` rather than read as either, because picking one by declaration order, category order, rank, or assertion count is how a guess becomes a confident answer.

This is what a reader needs and what validate returns. Process returns `RecognitionWithCorrections`, which adds how to correct the text.

inputFormat.description:
What the text was read as, when that is decided.

For a scheme without `render.surfaces`, the format recognized, when exactly one was. For a scheme with them, the output address, `surface/view`, of the view the text was read as, decided as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states: the same key that view's output has in `renders`. The form it happened to be read in is not reported. Absent when no one view is decided, as for text that carries the categories of more than one surface.

role.description:
Whether the text is spelled as a whole or a part marking: the role of the view it was read as, or, when no one view is decided, the role `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` decides for it.

Present only for a scheme that declares `render.surfaces`, and only when that role is decided, as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states. A request that names no output and gives no context role is written in its surfaces' defaults for this role. A context role the request gives, or the place a document gives the marking, decides the role it is judged and written in.

surface.description:
The surface the input was read as, by scheme scope id.

A caller that named a surface gets it back. A caller that named none gets the surface the recognized format declares, or with `render.surfaces` the surface whose categories the text carries, which tells it which part of a marking the text turned out to be. Absent for text that carries the categories of more than one surface, unless the caller named one.

unmatched.description: Input not accounted for as content, syntax, or permitted whitespace.

RecognitionWithCorrections.description:
What recognition made of an input string, with the corrections that turn it into canonical text.

The corrections are the edit script recognition read through: each names a span of the input, what it said, and the canonical text it was read as. An author's editor uses them to show what changed and where. A reader has no use for them, which is why only process returns this form.

corrections.description: Departures from canonical that recognition read through.

inputFormat.description:
What the text was read as, when that is decided.

For a scheme without `render.surfaces`, the format recognized, when exactly one was. For a scheme with them, the output address, `surface/view`, of the view the text was read as, decided as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states: the same key that view's output has in `renders`. The form it happened to be read in is not reported. Absent when no one view is decided, as for text that carries the categories of more than one surface.

role.description:
Whether the text is spelled as a whole or a part marking: the role of the view it was read as, or, when no one view is decided, the role `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` decides for it.

Present only for a scheme that declares `render.surfaces`, and only when that role is decided, as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states. A request that names no output and gives no context role is written in its surfaces' defaults for this role. A context role the request gives, or the place a document gives the marking, decides the role it is judged and written in.

surface.description:
The surface the input was read as, by scheme scope id.

A caller that named a surface gets it back. A caller that named none gets the surface the recognized format declares, or with `render.surfaces` the surface whose categories the text carries, which tells it which part of a marking the text turned out to be. Absent for text that carries the categories of more than one surface, unless the caller named one.

unmatched.description: Input not accounted for as content, syntax, or permitted whitespace.

RenderAssessment.description:
What a render did to the state it was given, bound to that state and that format.

Answered against the state actually rendered: what was emitted, what was left out, what collapsed into an equivalent, and what could not be written at all.

A caller that needs full-state preservation reads this. A caller that wants a human projection can ignore it and still get a useful string.

collapsed.description: Groups of facts that collapsed into one written equivalent.

conflicts.description: Fields that two assertions both claim.

omitted.description:
Facts this render did not write.

Some of them come back when the written text is read in the same context, because the scheme derives them from what was written: a fact a rule adds, a category's default, a value a part takes from its whole. The rest are lost to the string, such as a fact of a scope or a surface this render does not write, or one a field that writes only its own view's spellings has no spelling for (`view_only`). Either way the string is a projection of the facts, and a `'full'` render refuses any omission.

unrepresentable.description: Facts that cannot be written in this format at all, and outputs refused whole.

RenderFieldConflict.description: Two fields of one format that both claim the same assertion.

field.description: The field, by `name` or category id.

RenderResult.description:
The output of a render: the string, and what producing it did to the state.

The assessment travels with the string so that a convenience caller cannot accidentally treat a lossy projection as a transport. It is bound to this render of this state, not to the format in the abstract.

For a scheme that declares `render.surfaces`, one result can be composed from the outputs of every surface it writes, and this is what such a composed result holds. The string is composed exactly as `ProcessResult.rendered` is. The assessment combines the surfaces written: it lists a fact as omitted only when no written surface wrote it, and an unrepresentable or conflicting claim from any surface stands. Such a claim is never cancelled because another surface wrote something.

assessment.description: What this render did to the state it was given.

RenderResultsByFormat.description:
Renders of one state, one per output, keyed by output address.

For a scheme without `render.surfaces` the outputs are its formats, keyed by format id. For a scheme with them they are the views of its surfaces, keyed `surface/view` with each id percent-encoded, surfaces in declared order and each surface's views in theirs. Every view a surface's default names is one of its views, so a default has no entry of its own, and a format no view writes has none either.

On a process result it holds exactly the outputs the request named in `outputs`. An output that was asked for and could not write the state says so in its assessment rather than being left out, because a missing key would mean nobody asked for it.

RepairConfidence.description: Confidence assigned to a deterministic repair.

ReproducibleRuleSourceReference.description: Compact source join carried by a qualified rule reference.

providerId.description: Stable identifier for the source provider.

reproducibility.description: Whether the source observation can be reproduced byte-for-byte.

ReproducibleSourceReference.description: Reproducible source identity and mandatory attribution for an operation.

attribution.description: Attribution and license information for the observed source.

locator.description: Location from which the content was observed.

providerId.description: Stable identifier for the source provider.

reproducibility.description: Whether the source observation can be reproduced byte-for-byte.

RuleCondition.description: A single condition in a rule's `when` block. Can test category contents, processing context role, or concept presence.

category.description: Category to evaluate against. Also serves as a shorthand matching any concept in this category within when blocks.

has.description: Shorthand for has_concept: check if this concept is present

target.description: Which assertion set to evaluate: 'self' (default), 'context' (the whole marking), or 'contributors' (every set that fed an aggregate).

RuleConditionTarget.description:
Assertion set a rule condition is evaluated against.

- `'self'` (default): the assertions currently under evaluation.
- `'context'`: the assertions of the whole marking this one is part of. Such a condition has an answer only when the part has a verified whole, one that reads and is valid. Without one (no whole given, a whole that does not read, or a whole that reads but is invalid) the condition is unresolved, and so is any `all`, `any` or `none` around it whose answer depends on it. A rule whose `when` is unresolved never fires, changes no value, reports no error and offers no fix; a check rule (`require`, `require_any`, `restrict`, `forbid`, `exclusive`, `cardinality`) that the marking already meets still passes, and any other unresolved rule gives the part the `_whole_unverified` notice.
- `'contributors'`: each contributing assertion set that went into an aggregate, evaluated separately. The condition holds only when EVERY contributor satisfies it, and it is never satisfied outside aggregation, where there are no contributors to inspect. Use it to describe what must be true of every part of a document, which the merged set can no longer answer once the parts have been collapsed into one.

RuleContributorQuantifier.description: Quantifies a condition block over contributing assertion sets.

RuleReference.description: Identifies the exact resolved semantics of one policy rule.

ruleDigest.description: RFC 8785/SHA-256 digest of the canonical resolved rule content.

ruleId.description: Rule identifier within the owning artifact.

source.description: External source identity when the rule was not supplied inline.

RuleSourceReference.description: Compact source join carried by a qualified rule reference.

RuleWhen.description:
Conditions that trigger a rule. Supports shorthand forms:

- `string`: concept ID must be present (any category)
- `string[]`: any of these concept IDs must be present
- `object`: structured `{ any | all | none }` block, possibly nested

RuleWhenNode.description: A leaf condition or recursively nested boolean quantifier in a rule tree.

RuleWhenQuantifier.description:
A node in a rule `when`-tree: either a leaf `RuleCondition` or a nested quantifier (`any` / `all` / `none`) over further nodes.

The tree structure allows arbitrarily deep boolean logic within a rule's trigger condition. Leaf nodes test assertion or context state; inner nodes combine them with OR (`any`), AND (`all`), or NOT-OR (`none`).

all.description: Satisfied when every one of these nodes is.

any.description: Satisfied when at least one of these nodes is.

none.description: Satisfied when none of these nodes is.

quantifier.description: Combine contributor results; defaults to all. Requires target: contributors. Missing or empty contributors never satisfy the block.

target.description: Evaluate this entire boolean block within each contributor.

ScanLimits.description:
How far a scan got, and what stopped it.

A scan spends one work budget over a whole document: finding the regions a marking could occupy costs against it, and so does reading each one. A document large enough exhausts it, and a document that offers more regions than the scanner will hold is capped. Either way the answer is a shorter list of markings than the document holds, and a shorter list is indistinguishable from a clean one unless the scanner says so. For a scanner whose answer decides how a document is handled, that is the difference between "this document carries no marking" and "this document was not read to the end", so it is reported rather than inferred.

`complete` means the whole document was offered to recognition. `resource-limit` means the budget was spent or the caller aborted, and `limitHit` names which. `truncated` means the region cap was reached with budget to spare. `regionsFound` is how many candidate regions the scan considered, which is the number that makes a zero result legible.

limitHit.description: The ceiling that stopped the scan, when one did.

regionsCapped.description: Whether the per-document region cap was reached.

status.description: Whether the document was read to the end, and if not, why not.

ScanOutcome.description:
What `scan` returns: the markings it found, and how far it got.

An empty list is what a clean document and an abandoned one both look like, so the limit report travels beside the markings on every scan instead of behind a second call. A caller whose next step depends on completeness reads `limits`; one that only highlights matches reads `results`.

limits.description: How far the scan got, and what stopped it.

results.description: The markings the scan found, in document order.

ScanResult.description:
A single marking found during a scheme scan of free text.

One entry of `ScanOutcome.results` per detected marking occurrence in the document. `start`/`end` are offsets in UTF-16 code units in the input text, suitable for overlaying highlights in a rich-text editor. `result` carries what validate answers for the marking, so its facts and validity are available without a second call. `wrapped` is `true` when the marking was found inside an `embeddedMarkingStyle` wrapper pattern (e.g., a marking in parentheses).

end.description: End position in the (possibly stripped) input text

inner.description: The marking text inside the wrapper: the capture group of the scheme's `embeddedMarking` pattern. Present only when `wrapped` is true. Consumers that need to re-process the marking must use this rather than stripping delimiters from `marking`, because the wrapper shape is scheme-declared and is not always a pair of parentheses.

marking.description: The matched marking string (as found in the document)

result.description: What validate answers for this marking, read where it was found and in the role `role` names. A scan reads documents; it does not author them, so it carries no fix paths. A caller that wants to correct one region processes that region.

role.description:
Scheme-resolved structural role of this marking: `'whole'` (a document-wide marking: a page-top marking, a TLP document tag) or `'part'` (a per-region marking: a paragraph mark, a segment, a tag).

A marking found inside a wrapper is a part, because a scheme that declares a wrapper has said that is how a part is written. Otherwise, for a scheme that declares `render.surfaces`, it is the role recognition decides for it, the one `result.recognition.role` reports, and for a scheme without them, the role the scheme's `contextFormats` give the format it was read in. A marking with neither is a whole. Consumers should prefer `role` over `wrapped`, which only reflects wrapper syntax and not the scheme's whole/part intent.

start.description: Start position in the (possibly stripped) input text

type.description:
The output this marking is written in when the scan names no output format: `result.rendered` is written in it.

Without `render.surfaces`, the format id that read it, or when no single format read it, the scheme's default output, the `defaultRenderFormat` its metadata reports. With them, the view it was read as, the address `result.recognition.inputFormat` reports, when the form it was read in is one that view writes: its `format` or a case's format. A marking read in one form that carries more than one surface, such as an attribute list, is read as no one view; when the views that name that form all write it under one view id, it is written in them, and its type is that bare view id, the output format that writes each surface in its view by that id. Any other marking, one read in a form its view is only read in or read as no one view, is written in the default for its `role`, the `defaultWholeRenderFormat` or `defaultPartRenderFormat` its metadata reports, and that default is its type.

wrapped.description: Whether the marking was found inside a wrapper pattern (e.g., parentheses)

ScanStatus.description:
How far a scan got.

`complete` means the whole document was offered to recognition. `truncated` means the region cap was reached with budget to spare. `resource-limit` means the budget was spent or the caller aborted.

SourceReference.description: Records source identity and mandatory attribution for an operation.

SubjectContextRequirement.description: Conditional external relationship needed by a subject-context comparison.

acceptableValues.description: Context values that would satisfy the relationship, when known.

instruction.description: Conditional explanation of the external-state prerequisite.

SuggestResult.description:
What suggest answers: the concepts a picker may offer, and nothing about the marking itself.

How the current marking reads and whether it stands are what validate and process answer, and suggest does not repeat them. A caller that wants both in one round trip asks process for them with `suggestFor`.

suggestions.description: The concepts on offer, in display order.

warnings.description: Advisories raised while building the options, such as a concept source that could not answer in full. Empty when there were none. Advisories about the marking itself belong to validate and process.

SuggestResultsByCategory.description:
Suggestions for several categories, keyed by category id.

Each entry holds the options for its own category and no other, answered as if that category's own assertions were not yet chosen, so a picker can offer the alternatives to its current selection, not only what can still be added beside it. A label preset belongs to no category, so no entry offers one. `suggestForCategories` returns this, and so does a process call that names categories in `suggestFor`.

Suggestion.description:
A concept offered to the user in the suggest UI, with label, description, group, and current selection state.

Returned in `SuggestResult.suggestions`. `selected: true` means the concept is already in the current marking; clicking it again removes it. `order` controls display position within the group. `views` carries all render-format representations so the UI can switch formats without a second query. `source` distinguishes concepts from parsing the input (`'parse'`), preset shortcuts (`'preset'`), or alias matches (`'alias'`).

categoryId.description: The category the concept belongs to.

conceptId.description: The id of the suggested concept.

description.description: Secondary label (longer name or alternate view).

gated.description: True when this concept matches the active filter but is currently gated by the scheme's rules (a rule prerequisite is unmet, or a constraint forbids it). Gated suggestions are surfaced as non-selectable, explanatory rows so the user can see why the concept is unavailable. Only populated when the caller passes `includeGated: true` and a filter is active.

label.description: Primary display label in the current render format.

requires.description: When `gated` is true, the unmet prerequisite concept ids that would unlock this concept. Empty array when the concept is gated by a constraint with no specific prerequisite (e.g. mutual exclusion).

requiresDisplay.description: Resolved operational display (rendered marking view) for each id in `requires`, index-aligned, so the unlock row can read "add X first" with the marking rather than the raw id. `requires` stays as the machine keys.

selected.description: True if this concept is already in the current marking.

source.description: `preset` on a row that offers a label preset, whose `conceptId` is `preset:` followed by the preset id. A concept row leaves it unset.

plural.description: The word for more than one, such as `rules`.

singular.description: The word for one, such as `rule`.

tokens.description: The largest distance allowed between two spans, counted in whitespace-delimited tokens between their nearest edges.

TraceEntry.description:
One step in the engine's explanation trace: which stage acted, what it did, and which concept/rule was involved.

Lives in `ExplanationTrace.entries`. Consumers use the trace to render a "why was this marking produced?" breakdown. `stage` is one of `parse | repair | infer | validate | render`; `conceptId` and `ruleId` identify the specific element that drove the action.

action.description: What the stage did, as a short machine-readable token, such as `asserted`, `inferred`, `removed` or `unmatched`. An open string.

categoryId.description: Category the action landed in, when the acting rule declared one. This is the structured channel for the category: `detail` is human-facing prose and must never be parsed to recover it.

conceptId.description: The concept the step acted on, when it acted on one.

conceptName.description: Resolved operational display for `conceptId` (the concept's rendered marking view), so a "why" breakdown UI can show the marking rather than the raw id. `conceptId` stays as the machine key.

detail.description: A sentence describing the step for a person. It is prose and must not be parsed; the structured fields carry the ids.

ruleId.description: The scheme rule that drove the step, when one did.

stage.description: The pipeline stage that acted, such as `parse`, `normalize`, `repair`, `infer`, `validate`, `render`, `aggregate` or `context`. An open string.

triggerConceptIds.description: Concept IDs that triggered the rule producing this entry.

TraceInference.description: Inference recorded in an explanation trace.

conceptName.description: Resolved operational display for `conceptId` (the concept's rendered marking view), so a "why" breakdown UI can show the inferred marking rather than the raw id. `conceptId` stays as the machine key.

explanation.description: Why the rule added the concept, in words.

ruleId.description: The id of the inference rule that fired.

TraceRepair.description: Repair recorded in an explanation trace.

confidence.description: The confidence the scheme declares for the repair rule.

cosmetic.description: True when the repair changed only formatting and left the assertions as they were.

description.description: What the repair does, as the scheme describes it.

ruleId.description: The id of the repair rule that fired.

TraceValidationIssue.description: Validation issue recorded in an explanation trace: the constraint that failed and its message, and nothing else. The category, severity and concepts of the error it came from belong to the error, which a validate or process result reports in `errors`.

constraintId.description: The id of the constraint that failed.

UnrepresentableFact.description: A fact this format has no way to write.

conceptId.description: The concept that cannot be written.

detail.description: Human-readable detail, for a message rather than a branch.

reason.description: Why this format cannot write it.

UnrepresentableFactReason.description:
Why this format cannot write a fact it was given.

Closed, like the recognition-side reasons. `unframable` is a value carrying a character the syntax cannot frame; `reserved-literal` a free value equal to a fixed instruction beside it, which would read back as the other concept; `ambiguous-identity` a value indistinguishable from a differently typed one; `no-field` a fact this format's tree has no field for; `no-view` a concept with no spelling in this format's view; `value-lossy` a concept this format writes without its captured text.

UnrepresentableOutput.description: An output refused whole. Only a scheme that declares `render.surfaces` refuses one, because only its views choose a format by condition, and a choice that cannot be made is not a fact some format failed to write.

detail.description: Human-readable detail, for a message rather than a branch.

output.description: The output refused, by its `surface/view` address.

UnrepresentableOutputReason.description:
Why an output was refused whole, before any of its facts was written.

Closed. `unresolved-context` is an output whose choice of format turns on a condition the operation cannot decide, such as one that reads context the caller did not supply. `ambiguous-representation` is an output with more than one representation in force and nothing to choose between them, such as two of its cases holding at once.

UnrepresentableValue.description: Something a render could not write: one fact, or a whole output. `reason` tells the two apart, and only a fact carries a `conceptId`.

ValidateResult.description:
What validate answers about one marking: the facts it states once settled, whether they stand, and what a reader needs to show why not.

Validate is the reader's call. A host that displays a marking, gates on it, stores it, or hands its facts to an access check or a rollup calls it. The result carries no fix paths, no corrections to the text and no output beyond the one rendering, because a reader is not writing the marking. The author's call is process, and a `ProcessResult` is this result with the authoring answers added.

Each field means the same wherever it appears: on a validate or process result, on each region of a scan, in-process or over a wire.

Scheme and engine metadata (schemeVersion, schemeId) are not on the result; read them from `engine.version`, `engine.scheme.id` and `engine.scheme.version` instead.

appliedFixes.description:
Every change the engine actually made while settling the marking: a departure from canonical spelling or order that recognition read through, a repair, a fact a rule required, a handed-in fact settling removed, or text read in the other role from the one the request names. A removed fact is named with the reason it was removed, including a fact handed in with a derived source label that the run does not derive again. A requirement that conflicts with an existing concept is not added and appears in errors and proposed fixes, with no applied change. Repair never removes an author-stated concept. These are the reasons a marking can be `valid` while `inputWasValid` is false.

A departure from spelling or order is reported here without a position. On a process result, `recognition.corrections` reports the same departure with the span of the text it covers. They are one change seen two ways, so a display shows one of them, not both. The role departure, `_recognition_role`, is about the whole text: it has no span and no entry in `recognition.corrections`, so it is reported only here, and a display that shows corrections in place of this list still shows it.

assertions.description:
The facts the marking states, as the engine settled them.

Listed in print order: the order the rendered marking places each concept; a concept the rendering leaves out appears where it would print. A concept the rendering has no place for at all follows the others of its category, or comes last when its category has none, in the order the scheme declares.

assessment.description: The assessment of `rendered`: what it wrote of these facts, what it left out, what collapsed into an equivalent, and what it could not write at all. When `rendered` carries more than one surface, this is the combined assessment `RenderResult` describes. Read it before treating `rendered` as a transport.

displayColor.description: Portable scheme-derived display color for the settled marking. Embedding hosts may override this presentation default.

errors.description:
What the scheme's rules find wrong with the settled marking. An entry whose severity is `error` makes `valid` false.

No entry here points at a fix path: `suggestedFix` is set only on a result that carries the fix it names, and this result carries none.

inputWasValid.description:
True when the text or facts as given needed no change to stand.

Defined here once, and judged after the same settling as `valid`. A marking can be `valid` without having been valid as given: the engine settled it into one that stands. A result whose `inputWasValid` is false always says why: each change the engine made is in `appliedFixes`, and whatever it could not settle is in `errors`.

Right as written is judged against the view the text was read as, the one `recognition.inputFormat` reports, or for text read on more than one surface, the view each surface's part was read as. A fact settling adds, including a restored tier parent, counts against it only when that view writes the fact. A view that leaves the fact out writes the same text with the fact as without it, so the text was right already. Text read as no single view counts the fact when any view that read it writes it. Facts handed in with no text are judged against what a request that names no output writes them in, by the rule `rendered` follows.

Text is also not right as written when the request's context names a role and recognition decided the text is a view of the other role, as `recognition.role` reports. The result carries that departure in `appliedFixes` under `_recognition_role`, and `valid` is judged as it would be without it. A request that names its input format has said which view the text is: the text is judged as that view, and no role departure is raised. On a scan region and on a marking a document audit judges, the role the marking's place gives it stands for the context's role: a region found inside a wrapper is a part, and an audit judges each marking in the role it has in the document.

notices.description: The notices the scheme attaches to the concepts in `assertions`, collected the same way `SchemeEngine.collectNotices()` collects them. Always present, empty when the marking carries none, so a consumer can read the field without checking that it exists.

recognition.description:
What recognition made of the text: how far it got, what it read the text as, and what it could not account for.

Present exactly when there was text to recognize. Given facts, nothing was read, and the field is absent rather than carrying a made-up status about an input that does not exist. The same holds for every other result built from carried facts, notably a crosswalk's target.

rendered.description:
The settled marking, in one string.

It is written in the output the request names. With none named, a scheme without `render.surfaces` writes its default format, and a scheme with them writes each surface in its default for the marking's role, by the rule `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states. Every operation that returns this shape follows that one rule.

For a scheme that declares `render.surfaces`, the string is the output resolved on each surface the result writes, as `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` describes, in declared surface order and joined by `render.surface_separator`. An output that writes nothing adds nothing, and outputs written as XML attributes in one namespace merge into one attribute list. One refused output refuses the whole string, and `assessment` says which one and why.

valid.description:
True when the marking stands once the engine has settled it: read, repaired, completed by what the scheme's rules imply, and judged with no error left.

Defined here once, and every result that reports `valid` means this, whichever operation produced it and whichever door it came through. Reading is tolerant on purpose, so the engine settles what it can. Whether the text was right as written is what `inputWasValid` and `appliedFixes` answer; no request asks the engine to settle less, so validate and process give the same `valid` for the same input, context, surface and parts.

warnings.description: Advisories that do not affect `valid`, such as a deprecated concept. On a process result whose fix paths were not all proven, this carries a notice whose `ruleId` is `_fixes_unproven`, as `ProcessResult.proposedFixes` describes.

ValidationError.description:
A constraint violation detected during validation, referencing the constraint ID and a human-readable message.

Carried in the `errors` of every result that judges a marking. `constraintId` identifies the rule that fired; `message` is human-readable. When `severity` is `'warning'`, the violation is advisory and does not set `valid` to `false`. Use `categoryId` and `affectedConcepts` to highlight the specific UI elements involved.

Two of the ids the engine keeps for itself are for a fact a caller hands in that cannot be settled as given: `_missing_assertion_value`, a concept that takes a value handed in with none, and `_invalid_assertion_value`, a value the concept's encoding cannot read. Each is an error on the result, not a refused request: the fact is left out of the settled marking and named in `affectedConcepts`.

Another, `_exceeds_whole`, is a part that carries more than the whole it is read in: the whole does not cover a value the part holds, carries one the part does not allow, or, in a category a rollup pipeline resolves, would change if rolled up with the part. It is given only for a part that is valid on its own, read in a whole that reads and is valid. `affectedConcepts` names every finding, and no fix answers it. See `ProcessingContext.partOf`.

affectedConcepts.description: Concept IDs involved in this validation failure.

categoryId.description: Category ID this error relates to (when determinable from the constraint).

constraintId.description: The id of the constraint that was violated: a scheme rule's id, or an engine-reserved id beginning with `_`.

didYouMean.description:
The ids of the concepts the unread token was likely meant as. Never empty. They are ids for a program to act on, not spellings to show an author: `message` gives the same hint in words, naming the spellings.

Set only on an `_unmatched_token` error, which is about one token the engine could not read, and only when that token reads as a misspelling of some concept's spelling. The concepts named are tied for nearest, so their order ranks none above another.

Its absence is no evidence that the token is stray text. A token too short to judge carries none, and so does one equally near to too many concepts. A token that already spells a concept, apart from case, carries none even when it is also near another concept: it was left unread for another reason, such as where it stands, and naming a different concept would point the author away from a word they spelled right.

It is not a fix: nothing here has been proven to make the marking valid, and `suggestedFix` and the result's fix paths do not depend on it.

message.description: What is wrong, in words a person can act on.

severity.description: Severity: 'error' blocks validity, 'warning' is advisory. Default: 'error'.

suggestedFix.description:
The `message` of the proposed fix that answers this error, such as "Add CTRL-A".

Set only on a result that carries that fix in its own `proposedFixes`. A result with no fix paths, such as a `ValidateResult` or a scan region, never sets it, so a reader never holds a pointer to a fix it was not given.

ValidationSeverity.description: Severity assigned to a validation issue.

Vocabulary.description:
Author-facing vocabulary: an open map from a term key (e.g. "rule", "concept", "tag") to the display words. Term keys are not enumerated here; consumers pick the keys that matter to them.

Purely a presentation hint: nothing in the engine's evaluation logic reads it. Each consumer owns its own default map and calls `resolveVocabulary(source, defaults)` to merge.

Warning.description:
A non-blocking informational signal surfaced in a result's `warnings`.

Unlike `ValidationError`, warnings never affect `valid`. `kind: 'deprecation'` fires when a deprecated concept is asserted, and `replacement` names a suggested successor concept. `kind: 'rule'` fires when a scheme's authored `warn` rule matches the marking, with the rule's id as `ruleId`. `kind: 'notice'` is the engine speaking about the operation itself rather than about anything the scheme declares; its `ruleId`, when present, is an engine-reserved id beginning with `_`, the same convention a `ValidationError` follows.

A marking's warnings come in a fixed order: deprecations first, then the scheme's rule warnings in the order the scheme declares its rules, then the engine's notices. An aggregate's warnings are about the rolled-up marking, not about each marking that fed it.

categoryId.description: Category this warning relates to (when applicable)

conceptId.description: Concept this warning relates to (when applicable). A rule warning names one when the rule's `when` names exactly one concept the marking holds.

conceptName.description: Resolved operational display for `conceptId` (the concept's rendered marking view), for a consumer that shows the warning next to the concept. `conceptId` stays as the machine key; this is the human-visible string.

kind.description: Warning kind: 'deprecation' for a deprecated concept, 'rule' for a scheme's authored `warn` rule, 'notice' for the engine's own notice.

replacement.description: When kind=deprecation, the suggested replacement concept id (if any)

replacementName.description: When kind=deprecation, the resolved operational display for `replacement` (the successor concept's rendered marking view). `replacement` stays as the machine key; this is the human-visible string.

ruleId.description: The scheme rule that gave a `rule` warning, or the engine-reserved id of a `notice`. Absent on a deprecation warning.

WarningKind.description: Non-blocking warning category: a deprecated concept, a scheme's authored `warn` rule, or a notice the engine gives about the operation itself.

Win.description: A bounded proximity window. Exactly one token or character bound is present, so a windowed operation can never widen to the whole line accidentally.

description: Native operation result shapes used to validate typed expectations.

schemeScan.description: The result of a `schemeScan` case: the markings found and how far the scan got. A case passes only when the scan read the whole text, unless one of its assertions is on `limits.status`, which is how a case says it expects the scan to stop early.
